name: scans
title: Scans
description: A photographed or emailed document on its way into the books. The record is EVIDENCE and is never edited (docs/logic-decisions.md #8): the image is what an auditor actually wants, the OCR text is what a machine read, and the extraction is what a machine GUESSED. None of it posts anything. The write that matters happens when a human confirms, which creates a draft expense (or bill, or bank import) stamped generated_from scans/{id} and attributed to them -- so a weak extractor costs somebody thirty seconds of typing rather than putting a wrong number in the ledger. That boundary is why this can ship with no AI at all: the free path reads totals with regex over OCR text, an AI vision pass simply guesses better, and confirmation cannot tell them apart. content_sha256 makes re-snapping the same receipt land on the same scan, because the second photo of a crumpled receipt is the normal case, not the exception.

fields.name: content_sha256
fields.label: Content Hash
fields.help: Of the stored bytes. The dedup key: photographing the same receipt twice, or emailing what somebody already snapped, must not become two expenses.

fields.name: file_id
fields.label: Stored File
fields.help: Where the bytes live under the owner's files. The image IS the audit evidence; everything else here is derived from it.

fields.name: source
fields.label: Source
fields.help: Where it came in from. Capture has to happen at the moment the paper exists -- a receipt that needs a laptop later is a receipt that is already lost.

fields.name: category_hint
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: What the person capturing it says it is. Cheap at capture time, expensive to infer afterwards.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Status
fields.help: pending goes straight to extracted when a pass reads it in one go; processing exists for an engine slow enough that somebody would otherwise wonder whether it hung. error returns to pending so a fixed engine can retry the backlog. ignored is for the blurry duplicate nobody needs -- reversible, because 'ignore' should never mean 'lose'. confirmed is terminal: the record it produced is the thing to correct now, not this evidence of what arrived.

fields.name: ocr_text
fields.label: Text Read
fields.help: What the engine read. Kept even when extraction found nothing, because it is searchable and because it is how somebody works out why a reading was wrong.

fields.name: ocr_engine
fields.label: Engine
fields.help: Which engine produced the text and the guess. Recorded so a bad batch can be found and re-run when the engine changes.

fields.name: extracted
fields.label: Extraction (JSON)
fields.help: The structured GUESS: vendor, date, total, tax, line items. Stored, shown beside the image, never posted.

fields.name: confidence
fields.label: Confidence
fields.help: How much was actually found, not how sure a model claims to be. For sorting 'probably fine' above 'look at this one' -- never a threshold for acting unattended.

fields.name: confirmed_record
fields.label: Became
fields.help: collection/id of what a human created from this. Present means confirmed: one scan, one record, however many times anyone clicks.

fields.name: attempts
fields.label: Attempts
fields.help: Processing tries. A document that fails repeatedly stops being retried and starts being visible, rather than churning a paid extractor forever.
